claims.statement: Ask is a single deep agent built by build_agent() in app/ask/agent.py with a fixed TOOLS list of six tools (db_list_tables, db_describe_table, db_profile_column, db_query, search_graph, compare_fit) plus read_file and ls for skill reading; fetch_url is no longer among them. It has no subagents and no task tool, and tests pin the exact tool set.

agentkit/harness.install() registers a HarnessProfile disabling deepagents' general-purpose subagent for all supported providers, and harness.filesystem() replaces the default FilesystemMiddleware per agent so only the kept tools (read_file, ls for Ask) are registered; nothing that writes is exposed. The harness is shared in app/agentkit/ by Ask, Import and the proposal copilot.

Every Ask tool wraps its body in try/except and returns an error string instead of raising, because a raised tool exception would abort the whole run; compare_fit returns 'compare_fit failed: ...' or 'compare_fit refused: ...' strings, and the db_query and db_profile_column rejection and failure prefixes are a wire format that the retry limiter matches. tool_errors() (a ToolErrorMiddleware from app/agentkit/middleware.py, in Ask's stack and on every agent) is the backstop that turns a raised exception into a '<tool> failed: <ExceptionType>' string without the exception message.

Ask has four on-demand skills (funder-matching, funder-comparison, funder-shortlist-brief, news-brief) in app/ask/skills/, loaded by the model via read_file through a CompositeBackend that routes /skills/ to a virtual_mode FilesystemBackend while everything else is virtual StateBackend; skills hold procedure while matching judgement lives in compare_fit code. The news-brief skill uses db_query only: it gives a negative, fcra or governance story's main link as it is and does not fetch the page.

Ask's middleware order is filesystem, tool_errors, sql_retry_limiter, model_call_cap, CompareFitBudget, clear_old_tool_results, the model fallback and the cheap summarizer, then answer_audit only when settings.sql_audit_model is non-empty. The retry limiter is a before_model hook that counts failed or rejected db_query and db_profile_column results since the latest human message and at MAX_SQL_ATTEMPTS=5 appends a fixed give-up message and jumps to end; a test ties the prompt's number to the constant.

clear_old_tool_results (app/agentkit/middleware.py) clears old tool output once context passes 60,000 tokens, keeps the five most recent results, reclaims whole 20,000-token steps so the cleared set and cached prompt prefix move once per step rather than per call, and never clears compare_fit results; Ask, Import and the proposal copilot all use it, and tests pin the stepping, the bound and the compare_fit exemption.

The answer audit is an after_agent hook (answer_audit in app/ask/middleware.py over app/ask/audit.py), on by default with a Haiku model (disabled by setting off), that checks grain, filters, false zero and numbers only when SQL ran and an answer exists; it reads the SQL from the db_query message's artifact (falling back to an executed: line in the text); on a warning it appends a second AIMessage prefixed with a warning sign, scores answer_audit either way, and fails open on any error so it never blocks or edits the answer.

The SQL path has four layers: the catalog allowlist as data, a pure sqlglot validator that regenerates the AST so only the regenerated SQL executes, an executor running in a read-only transaction with local timeouts, caller role and prepare=True, and a renderer that emits cited rows, caveats and a sources block; db_query returns the SQL that ran as a tool artifact rather than in the text, and errors are translated into model-facing next steps.

The validator enforces a single read-only query of at most 8,000 characters: it rejects write nodes anywhere in the tree, INTO, locking and WITH RECURSIVE, cross-schema references and table functions, tables outside the catalog, non-allowlisted functions, row generators, placeholders, catalog casts, alias.* inside expressions and aliases in the reserved __prov__/__cite__ namespace; it resolves columns against the catalog schema, trims heavy columns from star expansion, aliases duplicate output names, and clamps LIMIT to a hard cap of 200 plus one row to detect truncation.

The executor wraps each query in conn.transaction() because the pool is autocommit, sets READ ONLY first and then transaction-local statement, lock and idle timeouts, applies the caller's role and claims via set_caller, uses prepare=True so the server refuses multi-statement strings, and limits concurrency with a semaphore sized by db_gate_slots (max(2, db_pool_max_size - 3)) so the checkpointer can still write.

Citation markers on SQL rows come from Column.cites declared in the catalog (kinds org, funder, activity, score, news), planned by the validator for projected id columns and rendered by render_rows as [kind:id] prefixes; the sources block is deduplicated, capped at 8 entries, derived from source link columns, and its grammar is a contract with the frontend pinned by tests.

Agent SQL runs as the signed-in caller under RLS: ask_access, the /agent dependency in AGENT_ACCESS, sets the agent_caller context variable, and the executor calls set_caller (role and JWT claims, transaction-local) after SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY, defaulting to anon when unset, so the connection returns to the pool as the owner; the catalog and validator remain the first guard. Import keeps the owner, and tools that use the shared pool directly, like compare_fit, must check access themselves via chat_user_id (matching.may_run). docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 3 and the CHANGELOG auth-plan row still describe the old owner-pool design and the unmerged branch fix/ask-sql-runs-as-caller, so they lag the code.

At boot lifespan._verify_sql_catalog raises when the catalog lists a table or column the database lacks, or when the authenticated role cannot SELECT a catalogued column or anon can read only part of a table; live tables that are in neither the catalog nor KNOWN_EXCLUDED are only logged at INFO, so a new table stays invisible to the agent until someone makes a decision; KNOWN_EXCLUDED declares sensitive tables such as checkpoints, users, threads, org_members and proposals.

test_sql_catalog.py asserts what the catalog must not contain: checkpoint and user tables, contact email and phone, embeddings; it also asserts cite kinds stay within the frontend union and that the import-time self-check fires on a dangling foreign key.

app/ask/instructions.md is the system prompt, with only {{TABLE_MAP}} substituted by render_prompt (failing at import if the file is empty); its rules require answering only from tool results, citing every database fact with a marker (computed figures labelled as computed), writing SQL for data questions with the table list in the prompt, schema description and column profiling, stopping after 5 failed attempts (db_profile_column's included), reporting empty results as what this user can see because queries run as the caller under row security, and delegating all fit judgement to compare_fit with its output repeated exactly.

Tests tie the prompt to the tools: every registered TOOLS entry must be named in the prompt and every citation kind a tool can emit (org, funder, activity, score, news, graph) must appear as a marker in the prompt.

Adding an Ask tool takes four edits: a never-raising, citing function in app/ask/tools/ (importable only by the agent builder under the R1 architecture rule), a line in TOOLS in app/ask/agent.py, a mention by exact name in instructions.md (enforced by test_prompt_names_every_registered_tool), and a label in frontend/features/ask/lib/toolLabels.ts, which is unenforced because humanizeTool falls back to a humanised name; that label map is shared with the proposal copilot's tools, and the pinned six-tool set in test_harness.py must also be updated.

compare_fit refuses callers who are not Sangam staff or the organisation's stewards or admins by checking matching.may_run with the request's chat_user_id before building any output, returns text (not JSON) of scored matches computed in code, and the prompt and skills instruct the model to relay a refusal and never assemble a match from db_query.

The SQL catalog allowlists 37 tables in CATALOG (37 Table entries in catalog.py), while KNOWN_EXCLUDED names 22 live tables (checkpoints, users, threads, org_members, proposals, funder_matches, import bookkeeping and others) deliberately kept out, so the boot check's undeclared-table log stays quiet about them but reports tables nobody has decided on.

The backend serves three agents registered in AGENT_NAMES: /agent (Ask), /ingest (Import) and /proposal (the proposal copilot); the proposal agent reuses the shared agentkit harness install, filesystem restriction and middleware helpers but has its own tools, and the frontend toolLabels map covers its tools.

compare_fit replies as line-per-fact text: without funder_ids it renders a header with per-tier counts and an 'unknown across' line, the top strong and medium fits (up to FULL_DETAIL_MAX=10) in full without summaries, every other scored funder as one line with its first gap, and separate not-scored lists for 'nothing in common recorded' and 'funder has nothing recorded (unknown, not a poor fit)'; with funder_ids it gives exactly those funders in full with summaries. The shape keeps the reply under deepagents' 20k-token eviction limit (60,000-character test budget) and pages cleanly, and tests pin it.

The Ask efficiency plan (docs/features/2026-10-16-ask-efficiency.md) has largely shipped in code: M2 (compact compare_fit shortlist, stepped tool-result clearing), M3 (the prompt's {{TABLE_MAP}}, validator-added __cite__ id columns, caveats once per request, 2,000-character cells for one-row results, SQL moved to the tool artifact) and M4 (fetch_url removed so Ask has six tools, db_profile_column errors counted by the retry limiter). The CHANGELOG records M3 and M4 as shipped while still tagging M1 and M2 as unmerged.

StaffLastLock and SaveQuestions are defined in app/ingest/middleware.py, not in Ask or agentkit; only Sangam Import wires them (staff_last_lock() on the entity-researcher and save_questions() on the catalog-writer in ingest/agent.py), and Ask's middleware stack does not include them.

model_call_cap(settings.ask_model_call_limit) is a before_model hook that counts AIMessages since the latest human message and, at ASK_MODEL_CALL_LIMIT (default 25), appends a fixed 'ask a narrower question' message and jumps to end, so a runaway question stops there rather than at recursion_limit.

CompareFitBudget is a wrap_tool_call middleware that enforces the once-per-question compare_fit rule in code: within the current turn it refuses a repeat with the same org_id and sorted funder_ids and any call beyond MAX_COMPARE_FIT_CALLS=3, returning an error ToolMessage without running the tool; a different funder set is allowed and a new human message resets the count.

Ask falls back to RESEARCH_MODEL through ModelFallbackMiddleware when a model call fails (omitted when it equals MODEL), and replaces deepagents' summarizer by name with cheap_summarizer so summaries are written by the UTILITY_MODEL tier at the strong model's thresholds; both helpers come from app/agentkit/middleware.py and are shared with Import and the proposal copilot.

Ask has no web tool: fetch_url was removed (M4, #247) so Ask fetches no model-supplied URL; app/ask/tools has no web module, the Tavily make_web_search now lives in app/ingest/tools/research_tools.py for Sangam Import, and the frontend still labels fetch_url for old chats.

db_query adds ids and sources for the model: the validator appends the id of each table read whose id is not selected (as __cite__ columns, skipped for aggregate, DISTINCT and set-operation queries) and appends __prov__ source columns, recording why it could not for aggregates, DISTINCT, UNION or CTE rows. render_rows then cites the rows and moves source columns into the sources block.

A table's caveats are given in full once per /agent request: ask_access sets a fresh caveats_given set, _caveats_for prints later results touching the same table as one line (rows are only what this user can see), and when the variable is unset every result gives them in full.

The old backend/app/agent/ package is split into app/ask/ (Ask-only builder, middleware, audit, prompt, skills and tools including the SQL engine) and app/agentkit/ (harness, shared middleware and model resolution used by every agent); tests/test_architecture.py enforces that only an agent's builder imports from tools/ (Ask's tools/sql engine exempt), that agents share code only through agentkit/ and core/ plus a short allowlist (Ask's SQL catalog is read by Import), and an 800-line cap from which the catalog is exempt by design.
